embedded_source_coverage.note: TRAP: 180/180 (100%) actor-embedded items carry a source uuid, but 0% of them resolve to any pack we will translate, so Babele's _stats.compendiumSource re-sourcing saves EXACTLY 0 chars here. Breakdown: 144/180 are WORLD uuids of the form 'Item.<16-char id>' — DocumentConverter._sourceCollection() requires a /^Compendium\./ prefix, so exact-source lookup is skipped outright. The other 36 are Compendium uuids pointing at packs that no longer exist in this install: alienrpg-corerules.alienrpg-talents-career (11), alien-evolved-starterset.alienrpg-weapons (13), alienrpg-corerules.alienrpg-talents-general (6), alienrpg-starterset.alienrpg-weapons (3), alienrpg-starterset.alienrpg-starter-talentscareer (2), alienrpg-corerules.alienrpg-weapons (1). WORKAROUND used in the proposed mapping: declare Adventure.items with expose:true. That publishes the Item EmbeddedCompendium into the per-document DocumentTranslationScope; EmbeddedCompendium's constructor then merges scopedPack.translations as the base entry layer for Actor.items, so embedded items match the Adventure-level item translations BY NAME. Measured coverage with that in place: 155/180 items (86.1%) and 48,181 of 52,998 mapped chars (90.9%). Per pack: core 144/149 items, 47,100 chars; starter 11/31 items, 2,282 chars (the other 20 starter items exist only in the CORE pack's item list and cannot be inherited across packs — each Adventure has its own scope). The 25 uncovered items (4,817 chars) must be translated inline under their actor: spacecraftmods 'Emergency Escape Vehicle II', talents 'Field Surgeon' / 'Take Control', weapons 'Knife' / 'Mk.16 150mm Banshee 70 Unguided Rocked Launcher', plus the starter-only 'Weyland-Yutani Key Card' and 'Kitchen Knife'. risks: FOLDER-NAME LOOKUP CRASH. module/helpers/rollTableData.mjs:7 and :24 do game.folders.contents.find(x => x.name === 'Alien Creature Tables' / 'Alien Mother Tables') and then read folder.contents WITHOUT a null check. Translating either folder name makes `folder` undefined and the creature sheet render throws a TypeError. The two system-pack macros compare t.folder.name against the same two literals. HARD RULE: those two folder names stay English. ('Alien Tables' and 'Alien Sub-Tables' are safe.)

cTableget() PREFIX FILTER. rollTableData.mjs:26 filters the Alien Mother Tables folder with x.name.startsWith('Critical Injuries'). Fully translating 'Critical Injuries on Xenomorphs' / 'Critical Injuries on Synthetics' empties the creature critical-injury dropdown and silently drops the actor's stored cTables selection. Use a prefix-preserving bilingual name ('Critical Injuries on Xenomorphs 异形重伤表') or leave those names English.

HARD-CODED TABLE NAMES IN SYSTEM JS. game.tables.getName() is called with literals at module/documents/actor.mjs:554 ('Panic Table'), :845 ('Stress Response Table'), :1067 ('Panic Response Table'), :1812 (localize('ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries') || 'EV - Critical Injuries'), :1815-1817 (localize('ALIENRPG.CriticalInjuries') || 'Critical Injuries' || 'Critical injuries'), :1830 ('Critical Injuries on Synthetics'), :1848/:1855 ('Spaceship Minor/Major Component Damage'), plus 'EV - 48a. LS - DANGER EVENT DETAIL' inside the core pack's own macro. All 11 exist in the packs. Two of them have an i18n escape hatch: with the client language set to cn the system first tries game.tables.getName('重伤') because lang/cn.json maps ALIENRPG.CriticalInjuries='重伤' — so that table may be renamed ONLY to exactly that string. ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries is MISSING from cn.json, so in Evolved mode the table must stay literally 'EV - Critical Injuries'. Everything else must stay English or the roll silently warns and aborts.

SKILL-STUNTS ITEM NAMES ARE A LOOKUP KEY. templates/actor/character-skills.hbs:15 emits data-pmbut='{{skill.description}}', and system.skills.<skl>.description is overwritten every prepareDerivedData with game.i18n.localize('ALIENRPG.Skill<key>') (actor-character.mjs:468). character-sheet.mjs:1117 then does game.items.getName(dataset.pmbut). So the 12 skill-stunts Items in the system pack must be renamed to EXACTLY the system lang file's skill strings for the active language (cn.json: 肉搏/指挥/科技/机械/操纵/医疗/机动/观察/驾驶/射击/耐力/求生). Any other translation — including leaving them English while the UI runs in cn — breaks the stunts popover for all 12 skills.

GLOBAL MAPPING LAYER, FIELD-KEY SHADOWING. registerMapping pushes a global layer (core/babele.js) merged into one effectiveMappings used by EVERY Babele-managed pack. MappingBlock#activeFields DELETES then re-sets a field by key, so a variant redefining `description` shadows Babele's built-in Item.description for any other system's item whose `type` happens to be 'weapon'/'armor'/'item' (dnd5e, pf2e...). Mitigated in the proposed mapping by adding an `exists` guard on the alien-only path to every description variant — do not remove those guards. Same reason the built-in Item/Actor `description` defaults are left in place at base level.

expose:true ON Adventure.items/tables IS ALSO GLOBAL. Every Adventure pack in the world now publishes its item and table translations into the per-document scope. For third-party adventures this is a benign superset (their actor-embedded items may now inherit item translations by name), but it is a behaviour change and could surface a wrong translation if an unrelated adventure has two same-named items meaning different things.

TABLERESULT KEYS: DUPLICATE RANGES. Default TableResult _identity exports by `range` ('1-6'). 38 results in these packs share a range with a sibling (37 core / 1 starter), so ExportKeys silently falls back to the raw 16-char _id for the second one. Matching still works (_id first, then range), but the translation file mixes readable range keys with opaque ids, and any upstream re-generation of result ids orphans those entries.

TABLERESULT documentUuid DOES NOT RE-SOURCE. All 45 real documentUuid values are world uuids ('RollTable.<id>', 'Macro.<id>'), so ReferencedDocumentFieldConverter always returns undefined. The 62 type:'document' results (60 core, 2 starter) that link to sub-tables must have their `name` translated explicitly AND kept consistent with the translated sub-table name, or the drawn link label and the table title will disagree (the link itself still resolves by id).

system.rTables / system.cTables DRIFT. These hold RollTable NAMES. If translated independently of the table names, the <select> loses its selection (selectOptions compares selected against the option key) and game.tables.getName(dataset.atttype) returns null → 'no crit table' warning. The proposed alienRollTableRef converter removes the drift by resolving from the same tables translation block — but it depends on Adventure.tables keeping expose:true. Also: 'None' is a sentinel compared verbatim (actor.mjs:2493) and must never be translated.

ADVENTURE IMPORT MERGES SHARED FOLDER IDS ACROSS PACKS. 'Alien Tables' (Btepu5tifRV0Pj7w), 'Alien Creature Tables' (LrpFZIuICZfNAr2v), 'Alien Mother Tables' (A0N3Ct1TQq9BuGk6) and 'Alien Sub-Tables' (w3xO69hCmTtYDF8d) have IDENTICAL _ids in all three packs, and 'Alien Evolved'/'Weapons'/'Creatures'/'Talents (Career)' repeat across starter+core. Their nameCollection translations live in three separate translation files; if they disagree, whichever adventure is imported last wins and folder names flip. Keep the folders block byte-identical across the three files.

STALE WORLD DOCUMENTS SHIFT NAME MATCHING AFTER A FIRST IMPORT. 144/180 embedded items carry _stats.compendiumSource = 'Item.<id>' pointing at a WORLD item. Once the adventure has been imported, DocumentConverter._sourceDocument() resolves those uuids via fromUuidSync and _sourceAwareData() rewrites the payload's `name` to the (already translated) world document's name before the generic-pack lookup. The English-keyed lookup then misses on that branch. It still works today because the current-compendium payload wins the mergeObject, but it is a real fragility if fallback ordering ever changes.

Babele's default Macro mapping exposes `command`; a translator editing 9,347 chars of JavaScript can break syntax with no validation and no error surface until the macro is run. Recommended: omit the `command` key from the translation files entirely (FieldMapping fails open on a missing key). If it must be translated, the literals 'Alien Mother Tables', 'Alien Creature Tables', 'EV - 48a. LS - DANGER EVENT DETAIL', 'Black' and 'Stress' must stay byte-identical.

DEAD/DERIVED FIELDS LOOK TRANSLATABLE AND ARE NOT. ~19,493 chars of item system.modifiers.*.label/.ability, ~9,065 chars of actor labels (system.skills.*.label/.description, system.attributes.*.label, system.header.*.label, system.general.special.label) and 4,005 chars of item system.notes ('[object Object]' x267) will show up in any naive extraction. Every one is either overwritten by prepareDerivedData, never rendered by any template, or corrupt data. Translating them wastes ~32.5k chars and, in the case of system.skills.*.description, would be a no-op that also hides the real lookup-key problem.

registerMapping MUST run in the babele.init hook. BabeleFacade#assertConfigurable rejects late registration once the runtime session exists (babele.js:291-293), and converters have the same constraint (babele.js:197-199). Registering from a `ready` hook silently throws.

PACK-LEVEL `folders` KEY IS A SECOND, UNCONTROLLED PATH. FolderTranslations.translateImportedCompendiumFolder (hooked on createFolder) renames imported world folders from the pack's top-level translation.folders payload, independently of the Adventure mapping's `folders` field. Do NOT put a `folders` block at the root of these Adventure translation files, or folder names get rewritten twice from two different sources.
